header.running_head: Entertaining People who visited Madinah Tayyibah

blocks.text: I may take for Rasulullaah ﷺ what he needs (to feed his guests).' Nistaas will then say, 'First produce a letter from your father (to authorise it).' Qais will then punch Nistaas on the nose and take the keys from him to provide Rasulullaah ﷺ with whatever he needs." Matters transpired exactly as Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) had mentioned and Hadhrat Qais (RA) took for Rasulullaah ﷺ a hundred Wasaq of provisions.[^1]

Hadhrat Maymoona bint Haarith (RA) (one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives) reports, "The Bedouins always came to Madinah and Rasulullaah ﷺ would instruct someone to take a Bedouin by the hand as his guest and serve him a meal. It was during a year of drought when a Bedouin came to Rasulullaah ﷺ one night. All Rasulullaah ﷺ had was a little food and some milk. The Bedouin ate everything without leaving anything for Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ brought the Bedouin for a night or two and he always ate everything. I therefore said, 'May Allaah not bless this Bedouin who eats the food of Rasulullaah ﷺ, leaving him without any.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then brought the Bedouin another night after the man had accepted Islaam and he ate only a little. When I mentioned this to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, 'While a Kaafir eats to fill seven intestines, a Mu'min eats to fill only one.'"[^2]
The practice of Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar (RA) During the Year of Drought

Hadhrat Aslam reports that during the 'Year of Ashes (destruction)', Arabs from all over collected in Madinah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed certain persons to go to these people and distribute food and gravy amongst them. These persons were Hadhrat Yazeed bin Ukht Namir, Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhramah, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdul Qaari and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Utba bin Mas'ood (RA). Each one of them was appointed to a particular sector of Madinah and they reported back to Hadhrat Umar (RA) every evening.

The Bedouins were stationed from the beginning of Thaniyyatul Wadaa up to the Raa'ij mountain and the areas of the Banu Haaritha, the Banu Abdil Ash'hal, the Banu Quraizah tribes. They even extended to the Baqee cemetery and some of them reached up close to the area of the Banu Salama tribe. They had virtually surrounded Madinah. One night after the people had had their supper with Hadhrat Umar (RA), he gave instructions that the people who eat with him should be counted. When they were counted the following night, they numbered seven thousand. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed that the families, the ill and the children who were unable to attend should also be counted. When they were counted, they were found to number forty thousand.
